title: Conventions of the contract's schemas
description: A draft-07 schema over the schema files themselves, checked by conformance/schema-checks.mjs beside the strict compile. It holds the conventions the README and CONTRIBUTING state: every schema names its dialect, its $id, a title and a description; no schema uses the `format` keyword (its meaning varies by validator, so the contract uses patterns); and every declared property carries a `$comment` beginning `stability: stable` or `stability: development`, optionally `; deprecated: <replacement>`, which is how the contract marks what it promises and what it is still deciding (a draft-07 `$comment`, because Bowtie showed a custom keyword is refused by strict validators elsewhere). Nodes under `if`, `then`, `else` and `contains` are conditions, not declarations, and are not held to the property rule.

stabilityComment.description: `stability: stable` is a promise under the additive rule; `stability: development` may change within the major and says so; `; deprecated: <replacement>` marks a field a writer should stop using, which is additive. Anything after another `; ` is free text.
